..summary: IRepoSettingsStrategy uses both 'update' and 'set' prefixes for semantically identical boolean toggle operations

evidence: updateVulnerabilityAlerts uses 'update' prefix while setAutomatedSecurityFixes and setPrivateVulnerabilityReporting use 'set' prefix — all three toggle a boolean feature on/off
detail.suggestion: Standardize on 'update' prefix to match the interface's primary get/update convention: rename setAutomatedSecurityFixes to updateAutomatedSecurityFixes and setPrivateVulnerabilityReporting to updatePrivateVulnerabilityReporting

..summary: GitLab force-merge path omits privilege-bypass warning that GitHub and ADO strategies both log

evidence: github-pr-strategy.ts:292 logs this.log?.warn(`Force-merging PR ... using admin privileges (bypasses branch protection)`) before force merge
ado-pr-strategy.ts:270 logs this.log?.warn(`Bypassing policies for PR ... (reason: ...)`) before force merge
gitlab-pr-strategy.ts:308-322 executes force merge with no warning log at all
detail.suggestion: Add a this.log?.warn() call before the force merge in gitlab-pr-strategy.ts, e.g. this.log?.warn(`Force-merging MR ${mrInfo.mrIid} immediately (bypasses pipeline requirements)`) to match the audit pattern of the sibling strategies.

..summary: shared/ imports sanitizeCredentials from vcs/sanitize-utils.ts, inverting the shared-as-leaf layering

evidence: src/shared/command-executor.ts line 2: import { sanitizeCredentials } from "../vcs/sanitize-utils.js" -- runtime import, not type-only
src/shared/retry-utils.ts line 2: import { sanitizeCredentials } from "../vcs/sanitize-utils.js" -- runtime import, not type-only
sanitize-utils.ts contains a single pure function that does URL/header credential masking with no VCS-specific dependencies
command-executor.ts has 46 importers, making this layering violation high-impact in the dependency graph
detail.suggestion: Move src/vcs/sanitize-utils.ts to src/shared/sanitize-utils.ts. Update the two imports in shared/ to use local paths ("./sanitize-utils.js"), and update the three imports in vcs/ (ado-pr-strategy.ts, github-pr-strategy.ts, gitlab-pr-strategy.ts) to use "../shared/sanitize-utils.js". This restores shared/ as a true leaf layer with no upward dependencies.

..summary: sanitize-utils.ts in vcs/ creates circular dependency with shared/

evidence: shared/command-executor.ts imports sanitizeCredentials from ../vcs/sanitize-utils.js
shared/retry-utils.ts imports sanitizeCredentials from ../vcs/sanitize-utils.js
vcs/ modules import extensively from shared/ (command-executor, retry-utils, errors, shell-utils, xfg-template)
sanitizeCredentials is a pure string function with zero VCS-specific dependencies — it only uses regex replacements on URL credentials and auth headers
detail.suggestion: Move sanitize-utils.ts from src/vcs/ to src/shared/ and update all import paths. The function has no VCS dependencies and is consumed by shared utilities, making shared/ its natural home.

..summary: getRepoDisplayName logic duplicated between repo/utils.ts and xfg-template.ts repo.fullName case

evidence: repo/utils.ts lines 66-74: getRepoDisplayName formats azure-devops as org/project/repo, gitlab as namespace/repo, github as owner/repo
xfg-template.ts lines 99-105: repo.fullName case repeats the exact same three-branch platform-specific formatting logic
detail.suggestion: Have the xfg-template.ts repo.fullName case call getRepoDisplayName(repoInfo) directly instead of reimplementing the platform-specific formatting inline.

..summary: extends-resolver.ts throws bare Error instead of ValidationError for config validation failures

evidence: Lines 16, 23, 29 throw new Error() for circular extends, missing group, and depth exceeded -- all config validation failures
Every other file in src/config/ (loader.ts, config-merger.ts, file-reference-resolver.ts, normalizer.ts, validator.ts) uses ValidationError for config-related errors
ValidationError is specifically designed for config validation failures and is imported by retry-utils.ts to classify as permanent (non-retryable)
detail.suggestion: Import ValidationError from ../shared/errors.js in extends-resolver.ts and replace the three bare Error throws with ValidationError throws. This aligns with the rest of the config module and ensures retry logic correctly classifies these as permanent errors.

..summary: src/shared/ imports sanitize-utils.ts from src/vcs/, reversing the expected dependency direction

evidence: src/shared/command-executor.ts:2 imports sanitizeCredentials from '../vcs/sanitize-utils.js'
src/shared/retry-utils.ts:2 imports sanitizeCredentials from '../vcs/sanitize-utils.js'
sanitize-utils.ts has zero imports itself - it is a standalone utility with no vcs-specific dependencies
detail.suggestion: Move src/vcs/sanitize-utils.ts to src/shared/sanitize-utils.ts. It is a pure string utility with no dependencies, and its only consumers outside vcs/ are already in shared/. Update the two import paths in command-executor.ts and retry-utils.ts accordingly.

..summary: switch in renderActionDiffLines lacks exhaustive default, unlike equivalent in lifecycle-formatter.ts

evidence: lifecycle-report.ts line 53: switch(action.action) handles 'created', 'forked', 'migrated' but has no default case after filtering out 'existed' on line 51
lifecycle-formatter.ts line 31-55: equivalent switch uses 'default: { const _exhaustive: never = result.action; throw new SyncError(...); }' pattern for compile-time safety
LifecycleActionKind is 'existed' | 'created' | 'forked' | 'migrated' — adding a new action would silently pass through the lifecycle-report switch
detail.suggestion: Add a default case with exhaustive never check after the 'existed' filter, matching the pattern in lifecycle-formatter.ts. Alternatively, restructure to use the same function for both reporting locations.

..summary: sync-command.ts uses module-scoped mutable state (_runScopeExecutor, _runScopeLogger) as implicit DI for free functions, contradicting the explicit DI used throughout the rest of the codebase

evidence: Lines 51-66: _runScopeExecutor and _runScopeLogger are module-level let variables, set once at the top of runSync (line 628-629) and accessed via getDefaultExecutor()/getLogger() throughout 20+ call sites
The free functions (logSettingsResult, applyRepoSettings, displayReports, runLifecyclePhase, runFileSyncPhase) all implicitly depend on this state rather than receiving it as parameters
This pattern prevents concurrent invocations and makes the dependency graph invisible at call sites - a developer reading logSettingsResult sees no logger parameter but the function uses one
detail.suggestion: Refactor the free functions to accept logger and executor as explicit parameters, or consolidate them into a class that receives dependencies via constructor injection, consistent with the pattern used in SyncWorkflow, RepositoryProcessor, and all other modules.

..summary: repo-metadata-provider.test.ts is in test/unit/shared/ but tests src/repo/GitHubRepoMetadataProvider

evidence: test/unit/shared/repo-metadata-provider.test.ts imports GitHubRepoMetadataProvider from '../../../src/repo/index.js'
All other repo/ tests (detector.test.ts, utils.test.ts) correctly reside in test/unit/repo/
detail.suggestion: Move test/unit/shared/repo-metadata-provider.test.ts to test/unit/repo/repo-metadata-provider.test.ts. Run: npm test to validate.

..summary: shared/ imports from vcs/sanitize-utils.ts creating bidirectional coupling with the utility layer

evidence: shared/command-executor.ts line 2: import { sanitizeCredentials } from '../vcs/sanitize-utils.js'
shared/retry-utils.ts line 2: import { sanitizeCredentials } from '../vcs/sanitize-utils.js'
sanitize-utils.ts is a pure string utility (20 LOC, zero imports from vcs/) that sanitizes credential patterns in strings
Coupling matrix shows vcs/ -> shared/ has 59 edges while shared/ -> vcs/ has 2 edges, both for this file
detail.suggestion: Staged reorg plan: (1) Move src/vcs/sanitize-utils.ts to src/shared/sanitize-utils.ts. (2) Update imports in src/shared/command-executor.ts and src/shared/retry-utils.ts to use './sanitize-utils.js'. (3) Update imports in src/vcs/github-pr-strategy.ts, src/vcs/ado-pr-strategy.ts, src/vcs/gitlab-pr-strategy.ts to use '../shared/sanitize-utils.js'. (4) Update test/unit/vcs/sanitize-utils.test.ts path to test/unit/shared/sanitize-utils.test.ts. (5) Run: npm run build && npm test to validate.

..summary: Multi-line JSDoc blocks on self-explanatory 1-3 line functions add noise without insight

evidence: base-processor.ts:117 has 4-line JSDoc '/** Common action literals shared by all settings processors. */' on a 1-line type alias
base-processor.ts:123 has 18-line JSDoc on isActiveAction which is a 1-line type predicate (entry.action !== 'unchanged')
normalizer.ts:107 has 4-line JSDoc 'Normalizes header to array format' on a 3-line function whose name already communicates intent
normalizer.ts:323 has 4-line JSDoc on applyFileLayer that adds context about merge semantics — this one is valuable; the pattern is inconsistent
detail.suggestion: Remove or reduce JSDoc on trivial functions where the name fully communicates intent. Keep JSDoc on functions with non-obvious behavior, edge cases, or API contracts. A good heuristic: if the JSDoc restates the function name/signature without adding new information, remove it.

..summary: IRepoSettingsStrategy includes branchExists() which is a repository query unrelated to settings management

evidence: branchExists(repoInfo, branch, options) is a repo-level query method placed on a settings strategy interface alongside get/update/set* methods that manage settings. It's only used in the processor to validate a default branch change.
detail.suggestion: Extract branchExists to a separate focused interface (e.g. IBranchQuery or IRepoBranchCheck) and inject it into RepoSettingsProcessor independently. This preserves ISP and keeps the settings strategy focused on settings operations.

..summary: ICodeScanningStrategy uses compound method names (getDefaultSetup/updateDefaultSetup) unlike sibling strategies' bare verbs

evidence: ILabelsStrategy uses list/create/update/delete, IRulesetStrategy uses list/get/create/update/delete, IRepoSettingsStrategy uses get/update, but ICodeScanningStrategy uses getDefaultSetup/updateDefaultSetup
detail.suggestion: Rename to get/update to match sibling strategy interfaces. The interface name ICodeScanningStrategy already provides the 'code scanning' context, so the 'DefaultSetup' qualifier is redundant in method names.

..summary: baseResult<TResult>() relies on unsafe 'as TResult' cast with only a comment-level contract

evidence: The function casts BaseProcessorResult to TResult with the comment 'All TResult subtypes only extend BaseProcessorResult with optional fields' - if any processor result type adds a required field, the cast silently produces an invalid object with no type error
detail.suggestion: Consider using a conditional type or runtime check to validate the result shape, or enforce the optional-only constraint with a mapped type

..summary: ResultsCollector.getOrCreate() mutates internal state behind getter-like name

evidence: getOrCreate() creates a new ProcessorResults entry and pushes it to the internal array when no match exists, hiding a side effect behind a name that starts with 'get'
detail.suggestion: Rename to ensureResult() or findOrCreate() to signal the mutation, or split into find() and create() methods

..summary: receiveMigration bundles ref cleanup, branch rename, repo creation, and mirror push in one 130-line method

evidence: Lines 424-557: receiveMigration sequentially handles (1) removing origin remote, (2) cleaning non-standard refs, (3) renaming default branch, (4) creating the repo via gh CLI, and (5) pushing mirror content. Each is a distinct phase with its own error handling.
detail.suggestion: Extract the four phases into private methods: cleanMirrorRefs(sourceDir), renameMirrorDefaultBranch(sourceDir, settings), createEmptyRepo(repoInfo, settings, tokenEnv), and pushMirrorContent(repoInfo, sourceDir, token, tokenEnv). The receiveMigration method becomes a 20-line orchestrator calling these in sequence.

..summary: Create/update formatting loop duplicated between code-scanning and repo-settings formatters

evidence: code-scanning/formatter.ts lines 38-61 and repo-settings/formatter.ts lines 73-95 contain the same chalk.green/chalk.yellow formatting loop for create/update changes, differing only in whether warnings are collected
detail.suggestion: Extract a shared formatChangeEntries(changes) helper in a common settings formatter utility that returns {lines, entries, creates, updates}. The repo-settings formatter can wrap it to add its warnings pass.

..summary: Module-level mutable variables _runScopeExecutor and _runScopeLogger create implicit boot-order dependency within sync-command.ts

evidence: Lines 51-52: let _runScopeExecutor and _runScopeLogger are module-scoped mutable variables set by runSync() (lines 628-629) and accessed by getDefaultExecutor()/getLogger() closures used throughout the file (e.g. logSettingsResult, displayReports, processSingleRepo).
Any function calling getLogger() or getDefaultExecutor() will throw if runSync() has not been called first, creating an implicit ordering dependency within the module.
detail.suggestion: Thread the executor and logger through the RepoIterationContext object (which already exists) and pass them explicitly to functions like logSettingsResult, displayReports, etc., eliminating the module-level mutable state.

..summary: mergePROptions uses verbose intermediate-variable-per-field pattern instead of spread

evidence: Lines 130-143: each of the 5 PRMergeOptions fields is assigned to a local variable (const merge = perRepo.merge ?? global.merge) then conditionally set on the result (if (merge !== undefined) result.merge = merge). This is 14 lines of mechanical code that grows linearly with field count.
detail.suggestion: Replace with a spread-and-filter pattern: `const merged = { ...global, ...perRepo }; return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(merged).filter(([, v]) => v !== undefined))` or use a utility that strips undefined. This maintains the same semantics (no undefined keys) with less ceremony.

..summary: ProcessorResult uses optional fields (prUrl, mergeResult, skipped, diffStats, fileChanges) instead of discriminated union variants, making outcome semantics ambiguous at consumer sites

evidence: types.ts lines 194-207: ProcessorResult has success, repoName, message as required, then 5 optional fields that are semantically correlated but not type-enforced (e.g. prUrl is only meaningful when success is true and not direct mode)
sync-workflow.ts returns at least 4 different shapes of ProcessorResult (auth skip, no changes, direct push, PR result) all through the same flat type
sync-command.ts line 156-162 determineMergeOutcome must inspect multiple optional fields to reconstruct what happened - this is glue logic that a discriminated union would eliminate
detail.suggestion: Introduce a discriminated union on a 'kind' or 'outcome' field (e.g. 'skipped' | 'direct_push' | 'pr_created' | 'error') so consumers can pattern-match on the outcome rather than inspecting combinations of optional fields.

..summary: attachRetryAfter/attachValidationDetails cast unknown error to access .stdout without type guard

evidence: Line 87: (error as { stdout?: string | Buffer }).stdout casts unknown error without checking if it has a stdout property
Line 106: Same pattern repeated in attachValidationDetails
These functions mutate the error object by adding retryAfter property via cast on line 94
detail.suggestion: Add a type guard function like isExecError(error): error is { stdout?: string | Buffer } that checks typeof error === 'object' && error !== null && 'stdout' in error before accessing. This is a single-function addition that replaces the unsafe casts.

..summary: diff-algorithm.ts casts item.type to string without verifying runtime type

evidence: Line 115: const type = item.type as string -- item is Record<string, unknown>, so item.type is unknown
Line 123: Same pattern for desiredItem.type as string
While preceded by 'type' in item check and followed by truthiness check, the value could be a number or object at runtime
detail.suggestion: Replace 'item.type as string' with 'typeof item.type === "string" ? item.type : String(item.type)' or add typeof check before the cast. This ensures the assertion matches runtime reality.
